intro: You wake up in a hospital bed. Your head is pounding.
On your wrist is a plastic band with raised letters. You run your thumb across them. Subject 23. Antibody positive. Do not sedate.
Your hands find your folding cane and your monocular on the bedside tray. You take them both.

intro.text: Attention. Containment breach at Clearwater Research Facility. All personnel evacuate immediately.
Sterilization protocol is armed. The site will be sterilized in {time}.
Subject 23, this is Kestrel, extraction team. Your blood is the cure. Get out of the building and reach our beacon at the forest edge. Listen for it.

headphones: Echo Protocol. Headphones are recommended. Sounds come from where things really are, left, right, ahead or behind.
intercom: All staff: report to decontamination. This is not a drill.
Remaining personnel: evacuate by the forest service road. Do not use the elevators.
Reminder: the sterilization countdown cannot be stopped from inside the building.
Containment teams have withdrawn. Seal doors behind you.
Infected patients respond to sound. Move quietly.
Power fluctuations reported on the research floor. Some doors may require manual power routing.

logs.title: Dr. Hale, day one
lines: Doctor Mara Hale, research log, day one. Subject 23 arrived today. Antibody levels unlike anything we have seen.
Bright kid. Asked me to give directions using clock positions instead of pointing. Twelve o'clock is straight ahead. I am going to remember that.

logs.title: Nurse Das, night shift
lines: Nurse Priya Das, night shift. 23 asked for braille labels on the medicine. Facilities said there was no budget.
So I made them myself with the label maker. Took an hour. Should have been done on day one.

logs.title: Officer Ortiz, door locks
lines: Officer Tomas Ortiz, security. The new door locks are sound-based. Chimes, knocks, tones. The director's idea.
If you're stuck at one, somebody probably left the answer close by. They always do.

logs.title: Dr. Hale, day nine
lines: Day nine. We isolated the antibody from 23's blood. We are calling it A-23.
One sample is in cold storage on this floor. If the worst happens, that sample must leave this building.

logs.title: Director Voss, trial memo
lines: Director Voss. The human trial proceeds tonight. Doctor Hale objects. Noted. Overruled.
The subject is to remain sedated during transport. The wristband will be removed.

logs.title: Nurse Das, the turn
lines: The isolation patients stopped reacting to light. But they turn toward sound. Every single one.
Keep the halls quiet. Walk, don't run. Soft feet.

logs.title: Officer Ortiz, field notes
lines: They hear everything. The slow ones groan. The crawlers scrape along the floor and can't work a door handle.
The fast ones breathe like they ran a mile. You hear that rasp, you find a locker and you hide.

logs.title: Dr. Hale, day twelve
lines: It's out. Voss sealed the labs with us inside.
I'm hiding the door codes where 23 can find them. Braille labels, beep recorders, the old phone line. 23 will know what to do.

logs.title: Director Voss, to oversight
lines: To the oversight committee. Sterilization is regrettable but necessary.
Subject 23 is an acceptable loss.

logs.title: Nurse Das, supplies
lines: I left juice boxes and bandages anywhere I could reach. Running wears you out, and when you're worn out you breathe loud.
Drink something. Catch your breath. Then move.

logs.title: Officer Ortiz, screamers
lines: Screamers. Thin and loud. When one wails, every one of them in earshot comes running.
If you hear the wail, don't wait around to see who answers.

logs.title: Dr. Hale, last entry
lines: 23, if you are hearing this: you are not an acceptable loss. You never were.
You are the reason any of us has a chance. Get out. And if you can, take A-23 with you.

memos: A memo, read aloud: Reminder, all staff. Clock directions only when guiding patients. Twelve is straight ahead.
A memo, read aloud: The cafeteria will be closed until further notice. Do not feed the patients in isolation.
A memo, read aloud: Facilities request. Please stop propping fire doors open with chairs.
A memo, read aloud: To whoever keeps leaving juice boxes in the supply closets. Thank you. Signed, everyone.
A memo, read aloud: Sound locks are now active on secure doors. Staff will receive the chimes by voice recording.
A memo, read aloud: Shuttle to the forest service road leaves from the loading dock every hour.

clues.memo: A memo is taped here. It reads: New code for the {door}: {code}. Do not write it down. Someone wrote it down anyway.
clues.phone_ring: A telephone is ringing on the {fixture}.
clues.phone: You pick up the phone. A recorded voice says: If anyone can hear this, the code for the {door} is {code}. Again: {code}.
clues.recorder_beeps: An old voice recorder labeled {door}. You press play. Count the beeps: each group of beeps is one digit, and a long tone means zero.
clues.braille: A braille label is fixed to the {fixture}. Your fingers read the {door} code: number sign, then {dots}.
clues.braille_card: Your braille reader card confirms the digits: {code}.
clues.braille_nocard: That's a number sign, so the letters a through j stand for the digits 1 through 9, and then 0.
clues.largeprint: A large-print sign is taped to the {fixture}. Through your monocular you read: {door} code, {code}.
clues.melody: A music box with a raised-letter tag: Chime for the {door}. Repeat it with the arrow keys. It plays the chime now.
clues.rhythm: A voice recorder labeled Ortiz, the knock. It plays the secret knock for the {door}. You will tap it back with the Space bar.
clues.breaker: A breaker panel with a raised-letter note: Door power for the {door} is on {rule}.

breakerRules.lowest: the circuit with the lowest hum
breakerRules.highest: the circuit with the highest hum

radio.noBattery: The radio is dead. It needs a battery.
radio.open: Radio crackles. Kestrel here. Go ahead, 23.

steps.operator: Kestrel here. Who's on this channel?

choices.text: This is Subject 23. I'm the patient with the antibody.
choices.reply: Copy, 23. Good to hear your voice. We're holding at the forest edge.

steps.operator: Head for the red exit signs. You'll see them past the lobby.

choices.text: I can't rely on signs. Please give me compass directions and how many rooms.
choices.reply: Understood. Thanks for telling me. Here's your route.

steps.operator: Command says the sterilization clock can't be changed.

choices.text: I'm carrying the cure in my blood. Ask command to hold the clock so I can get out safely.
choices.reply: You make a good case. Stand by. Command agrees to hold the clock. You have extra time.

radio.later: Kestrel here. Reading you, 23. Here's what I can see from the facility plans.

win: You step through the gap in the fence. Strong hands guide you toward the helicopter.
You press the cold case into Kestrel's hands. Antibody Sample A-23. The cure, and you, are safe.
Behind you, the facility goes silent. Ahead of you, the world gets a second chance.
partial: You step through the gap in the fence and the extraction team pulls you aboard.
You made it out. Without the sample, the researchers will have to start again from your blood. It will take longer, but there is still hope.
secret: You step through the gap in the fence, the antibody case under your arm.
You also carry every recording. Hale, Das, Ortiz, even Voss. The whole truth about Clearwater.
Kestrel listens to one log and goes quiet. Then they say: Nobody is calling you an acceptable loss again. Secret ending found.
sterilized: The countdown reaches zero. A deep thunder rolls through the building.
Clearwater Research Facility is sterilized. Try again, 23. You know the way a little better now.
infected: The bites are too many, even for your antibodies. Your strength fades.
The infection wins this time. Try again, 23. Move quietly and pick your fights.

downed: You wake up in the {room}, aching. Your antibodies fought off the bite, but it took a toll. Infection {infection} of {max}.

tutorial.intro: Welcome to the practice room. Here the clock is stopped and the dummy can't hurt you. Press R any time to hear an instruction again.

steps.say: Press the Up arrow, or W, to take a step forward.
Good. You heard your footsteps on tile. Now press the Right arrow, or D, to turn right.
Now press the Left arrow, or A, to turn left.
Press the Down arrow, or S, to step backward.
Press C for your compass. It tells you which way you face and where you are.
Press Q to ask: where am I, and what can I do here?
Press P to send an echolocation ping. Listen to the echoes. Close walls echo fast and bright. Doorways sound like open air.
Press L to listen around you. You'll hear what is making sounds and where.
There is a cabinet in one corner of this room. Walk until it is within reach, then press Space or Enter to search it.
Press I to open your inventory. Use the Up and Down arrows to browse, and press I again to close it.
Press T to hear the time remaining. In a real game, the facility is on a countdown.
There's a door in the east wall. Walk through it. If the door is closed, walking into it opens it.
A training dummy is in this room. It groans like a zombie, but it can't hurt you. When it grabs you, press F to fight. Hit it twice.
Lockers let you hide. Walk next to the locker in this room and press E.
While hidden, zombies lose track of you. Press E again to come out.

Hold Shift while you walk to run. It is faster, but loud. Hold Control while you walk to sneak. It's slow, but quiet. Press V to switch between walking, sneaking and running if holding keys is hard. Try moving now.
During a real game, H gives a hint, but each hint costs a little time. Z tells you your health and noise. M reads the map. X taps your cane ahead. Press H now to try it.
To pause, hold the Escape key for about one and a half seconds. A quick tap won't do anything. Try it now.
Last one. Listen for the beacon. It's beeping beyond the doorway on the far side of this room. Walk to it and step through to finish.

controlsHelp: Up and Down arrows, or W and S: step forward and back. Left and Right arrows, or A and D: turn.
Space or Enter: interact. Open doors, search, pick up, read and use.
R repeats the last message. Shift plus R repeats the whole room description.
Q: where am I and what can I do. C: compass. L: listen around you. P: echolocation ping. X: tap your cane ahead.
I: inventory. H: hint, which costs a little time. T: time remaining. Z: health and noise. M: the tactile map.
Hold Shift to run, which is loud. Hold Control to sneak, which is quiet. V switches between walk, sneak and run.
F: fight. E: hide when a locker or hiding spot is within reach.
Hold Escape for one and a half seconds to pause. Slash or F1: hear these controls again.
